plan.curriculum: Design and Technologies, Levels 5 and 6: evaluating a product and process against criteria and making improvements; English, Level 5: giving and responding to feedback on a spoken presentation
plan.shape: 15 minutes explicit, 40 minutes team time: Lucas's pitch again to judge, kind, specific and helpful feedback on Pocket Pal, a quick round, then rehearsal swaps with the Shark Scorecard and one final fix
plan.criticalFeature: helpful feedback names one exact thing and says what to do; a team listens, then fixes one thing rather than arguing or starting again
decisionPoints: the choice check: what to do with feedback
the exit board: helpful feedback on a new pitch
plan.anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 7? Say: a pitch has six parts and ends by asking the sharks to invest. Your team gives you a part to learn today.

studentTools: Each team's prototype, poster, cue cards and business plan
manipulatives: One Shark Scorecard per team, for scoring the team they watch
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Team pairs for the rehearsal swaps written on the board
Kind. Specific. Helpful. One glow, one grow.
The Shark Tank Day must-haves: business plan, prototype, poster with the price, cue cards
videos: Glossy Boys on Shark Tank Australia, watched again from Session 3 (youtube.com/watch?v=ie2Q1srSpk0)

example.prompt: Make this feedback helpful: It's good.
steps: Name the exact part: the hook.
Say why: it made me want to listen.

items.prompt: Rewrite each one so it is kind, specific and helpful.
answers: e.g. The demo was hard to see. Hold it up higher.
e.g. Slow down in the problem part so we catch every word.
e.g. I liked how the price came before the ask; it made sense.

items.prompt: Which feedback would help a team most?
options: Your ask said buy. Ask the sharks to invest instead.
items.explain: The second. It names the exact part, the ask, and says what to change.

steps: Ask: is it made from things already used?
The whole pocket is old jeans.

evidence from the Token Test or survey

steps: Practise the ask, eyes up from the cue card.
Rehearse once more to check it.
example.answer: Practise the ask with eyes up, then rehearse again.

items.prompt: The most useful feedback our team got was... What will we fix?
items.answer: A specific piece of feedback and one matching fix.

sections.title: Plan the layout
sections.intro: Shops put the thing they most want you to see at eye level and in the middle. Your stall can do the same.

example.prompt: Where should Pocket Pal's team put the prototype and poster?
steps: The prototype is the star: front and centre, where sharks can touch it.
The poster stands up behind it, at eye level.
The price on the poster is big and easy to read.
example.answer: Prototype front and centre, poster behind at eye level, price easy to read.

items.prompt: Draw a bird's-eye plan of your stall. Label the prototype, poster and where your team stands.
items.answer: A labelled plan with the prototype at the front, the poster visible and the team beside, not in front of, the table.

items.prompt: Explain one choice in your plan. Why will it help the sharks invest?
items.answer: e.g. The prototype is at the front so sharks can try it, and trying it shows it works.

slides.notes: Dress rehearsal, the last session before Shark Tank Day. One line: today every team pitches, gets feedback, and fixes one thing.

Team pairs for the swaps on the board. Prototypes, posters and cue cards out. Cue the Glossy Boys clip. Print the Worksheet one per team, one Shark Scorecard per team, plus a few Extension and Supported copies.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning how feedback makes our product and pitch better.
successCriteria: I can give feedback that is kind, specific and helpful.
I can score a pitch with the shark checks.
I can use feedback to make one improvement before Shark Tank Day.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Shark Tank Day is next Monday. Today is the dress rehearsal.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Fifteen minutes with me, then forty minutes of rehearsing and fixing.
notes.prep: 15 minutes explicit, 40 team time. SC1 helpful feedback for all; SC2 scoring is the core; SC3 the fix. Anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.

slides.title: Judge Lucas's pitch
slides.prompt: Turn and tell: one exact thing Lucas did well.

notes.answer: open - listen for an exact part, like the demo or the hook
beats: PLAY 0:00 to 3:00 again. The player stops itself.
SAY: You're the shark now. Watch for one exact thing he does really well.
ASK: What's one exact thing Lucas did well?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: an exact part: his hook, the demo, knowing his customers
SCAN for an exact part, not just good.
80%+ -> cold call one pair: what would you tell them to improve?
Less -> ask: which part exactly? re-ask.
ASK: Thumbs: was that feedback about an exact part?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
trap: saying it was good, with no part named.
Fix: ask which part, student names the hook, demo or ask.
notes.prep: Launch. A rewatch with a new job: feedback. Grade 5s saw this clip in Session 3; he got a $75,000 deal.
notes.sources: Glossy Boys, Shark Tank Australia; SmartCompany on the deal.
notes.care: Anyone can wear nail polish. Stop any teasing at once.

slides.meaning: Information about what is working and what to improve.
slides.example: Your demo was hard to see. Hold it higher. That's helpful feedback.

notes.answer: information about what is working and what to improve
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Feedback. Say it with me. Feed-back.
SAY: Good feedback is kind, specific and helpful.
It names one exact thing and says what to do.
ASK: It's good. Is that specific?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: no
ASK: Thumbs: is Change it specific?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs down
trap: thinking feedback means saying what's wrong.
Fix: one glow and one grow, every time.
notes.prep: One key word. Glow and grow is the routine for the swaps.

rows: Glow: your hook made me laugh and want to listen.
Grow: look at the sharks when you say the ask.
Grow: hold Pocket Pal up so everyone can see the demo.

notes.answer: name one exact part and say what to do
beats: POINT to the Not helpful column.
SAY: These tell the Pocket Pal team nothing. What would they even change?
POINT to the Helpful column.
SAY: Each one names an exact part and says what to do. Kind, specific, helpful.
ASK: Score Pocket Pal on Upcycled, 1 to 3.
5 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 3, it's all old jeans
ASK: Write one grow for my Pocket Pal pitch from last week.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: an exact part and what to do
trap: a glow that only says good job.
Fix: ask which part was good and why, student rewrites.
notes.stretch: Why might a grow help a team more than a glow?
notes.help: Frame: I liked ... because ... Next time, try ...
notes.prep: The model for SC1. Students heard the Pocket Pal pitch in Session 7, so their grow can be real.

slides.title: Helpful or not?
slides.pivot: ask: which exact part, and what to do? then re-ask
slides.followUp: cold call one board: how would you make it helpful?

items.text: Hold Pocket Pal up when you say what it's made from.
items.answer: Helpful - exact part and what to do
Not helpful - unkind and not specific

items.text: Slow down in the problem part. You rushed it.
items.answer: Helpful - exact part and what to do

items.text: Your tagline was so catchy, I'm still saying it.

say: Quick round. Write helpful or not helpful
trap: calling a nice comment helpful when it names nothing.
Fix: ask what the team would change, student re-judges.
notes.stretch: Rewrite each not helpful one so it's helpful.
notes.help: Keep the Kind. Specific. Helpful. table on the board.
notes.prep: First decision point: telling helpful from vague feedback. Brisk. SC1. Six items, about 5 minutes.

slides.title: What do you do with feedback?
slides.prompt: Your team hears: your demo was hard to see. Point to A, B or C.

options.misconception: defends the pitch instead of listening

options.text: Hold the product higher and face the audience
Drop the demo from the pitch
options.misconception: removes the part instead of fixing it

notes.answer: B - fix the exact part the feedback named
beats: SAY: Feedback is a gift, even when it stings.
ASK: What do you do?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: B
SCAN pointing fingers, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: why not C?
Less -> back to the Pocket Pal strap: fix the part, keep the idea. Re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers are scanned.
SAY: B. Fix the exact part, and keep the demo.
Sharks love seeing it work. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing C because the demo caused the problem.
Fix: ask what makes a demo hard to see, student fixes that part.
notes.prep: Second decision point. Same idea as build, test, fix in Session 5. Under 80% means model a calm thank-you before the swaps.

slides.title: Rehearse, score, fix
slides.task: Pitch to your partner team. They score you with the Shark Scorecard and give one glow and one grow. Swap. Then fix one thing and check your must-haves.
slides.where: Your team table, Scorecard and Worksheet
slides.frame: I liked ___ because ___. Next time, try ___.
slides.extendedTask: a rehearsal swap with a scored Shark Scorecard, one glow and one grow given and received, and one fix made

notes.answer: every team pitches once, scores once, fixes one thing
beats: SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Everyone, together, on three: Pitch. Score. Fix.
TIME 40 minutes: two swaps 16, fix 14, must-haves 5, full run 5.
SAY: 90 seconds to pitch, 3 minutes to score and give a glow and a grow.
TIME at 30: stop everyone.
ASK: Thumbs: has your team made its fix?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
CIRCULATE. Ask: what was your grow, and what did you change?
trap: arguing with the feedback instead of fixing.
Fix: thank them, choose one fix, rehearse it.
notes.stretch: Extension: plan your stall layout so sharks notice what matters.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: glow and grow frames. Sit in on the team's first swap.
notes.prep: Every must-have stored together and named today: plan, prototype, poster with the price, cue cards. Shark Tank Day is Monday 7 December.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A team pitches: Ever lost a sock? Buy our Sock Buddy!
Write one kind, specific, helpful piece of feedback for them.

notes.answer: e.g. Grow: ask the sharks to invest, not buy. Glow: the question hook works.
beats: SAY: A new pitch. Work on your own.
ASK: Write one kind, specific, helpful piece of feedback.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: names an exact part and what to do
RECORD who writes good or bad with no part named.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC1, with the buy-not-invest slip as the expert catch. One board per student.
